title: 2011 AMC 10B Problem 7
statement: The sum of two angles of a triangle is \(\frac{6}{5}\) of a right angle, and one of these two angles is \(30^{\circ}\) larger than the other. What is the degree measure of the largest angle in the triangle?

solutions.text:
The two angles add to \(\frac 65 \cdot 90 = 108.\) This makes the other angle \(180-108=72.\) Then, if the larger of the two angles is \(x\) then the smaller of them is \(x-30\) so their sum is \(2x-30=108,\) making \(x=69.\)

This means no angle is larger than \(72,\) making the largest equal to \(72.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Convert \(\dfrac65\) of a right angle to degrees
Compare the third angle with the two angles whose sum and difference are known
